body.heading: Who owns Baskin-Robbins?
body.text: Baskin-Robbins is owned by Inspire Brands, a large US restaurant company. Inspire bought Dunkin' Brands, the parent of both Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins, in 2020 in a deal worth about $11.3 billion. That put Baskin-Robbins under the same roof as Dunkin', Arby's, Sonic, Buffalo Wild Wings and Jimmy John's.

body.heading: Backed by Roark Capital
body.text: Inspire Brands itself is backed by Roark Capital, an Atlanta-based private equity firm focused on franchised and restaurant businesses. So Baskin-Robbins is ultimately part of a big, privately held restaurant group rather than a standalone public company.

body.heading: A long history
body.text: Baskin-Robbins was founded in 1945 in Glendale, California, by brothers-in-law Burt Baskin and Irv Robbins, who merged their two ice cream shops. It grew into one of the world's largest ice cream chains, famous for its '31 flavors', before becoming part of Dunkin' Brands and then Inspire Brands.
